title: The Harbor of the Palatinate
premise: In 1913, Sebastian Pemberton drives for Lady Constance Harrow, a suffragist whose correspondence Sebastian reads before delivery — a habit that has made her the quiet keeper of a movement's secrets. When a sealed letter arrives implicating the Harrow family in a cover-up of a dockworkers' massacre being rewritten by government historians, Sebastian discovers that history is not something that happens elsewhere: it is being forged in her employer's parlor. As she races to preserve testimony from dying witnesses while evading both the police and the family she has come to love as her own, Sebastian must choose between loyalty and truth, and between a cautious love with a radical printer and the safe obscurity she always believed was her lot. The book ends with her testimony entered into the record at cost of her position and nearly her life — but with the official history cracked open, and a found family reassembled around a printing press rather than a great house.
about_author: Ansel Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing suffrage-era letters and learned that the margins of history are written by its couriers. This is their third novel, all concerned with people who carry other people's words.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Paper
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet her routine: driving Lady Constance through London, steaming open letters, filing secrets no one knows she keeps. She believes history happens to important people, elsewhere. A sealed letter with a government crest arrives; she reads it despite an unfamiliar wax seal, and finds the Harrow name beside the word 'Wapping.' Beat: unease beneath competence.

chapters.title: What the Driver Knows
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She investigates quietly, cross-referencing old letters about a 1910 dock strike and seven men officially 'lost at sea.' Lady Constance's warmth toward her feels suddenly like surveillance or like trust — she can't tell which. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that she stands outside history.

chapters.title: The Printer on Fetter Lane
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Following a name from the letter, she meets Elias Vane, a radical printer who lost a brother at Wapping. Their sparring over evidence and ethics sparks mutual recognition: two people who traffic in other people's words. Beat: reluctant alliance, first flicker of attraction.

chapters.title: Lady Constance's Silence
chapters.summary: Constance's POV. She knows what the letter means and has known for years; her suffragism is partly penance. She tests Sebastian's loyalty with small errands, torn between protecting the girl she thinks of as a daughter and burying the family crime. Beat: love entangled with guilt.

chapters.title: Seven Names
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Elias produces a list of Wapping witnesses; three are still alive, one dying in a Stepney lodging house. Sebastian realizes the victors' historians are already interviewing survivors — and steering them. Beat: the race acquires a clock.

chapters.title: The Lodging House in Stepney
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She takes testimony from Maggie Doyle, a widow who saw the militia open fire. The interview is interrupted by a polite man from the Home Office who offers Maggie money for her silence. Sebastian hides the deposition pages in her corsetry. Beat: fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: An Offer from the Family
chapters.summary: Sir Edmund Harrow's POV. He summons Sebastian, offers her a permanent post and a cottage, and mentions — gently, terribly — that he knows she opens the mail. He asks nothing explicitly. Everything is implied. Beat: gilded threat; duty wearing kindness's face.

chapters.title: Letters We Never Sent
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She and Elias grow close over late nights transcribing testimony; he shows her letters his brother wrote that mirror her own unsent drafts home. A near-kiss interrupted by news: Maggie Doyle has been found drowned. Beat: tenderness shadowed by grief and guilt.

chapters.title: The Archive at Kew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Using a forged reference, she accesses official records and finds the Wapping inquest file already thinned — pages razored out, replaced with a historian's tidy summary. She photographs what remains with a borrowed camera. Beat: cold fury; the enemy is not a man but a method.

chapters.title: Constance Breaks
chapters.summary: Constance's POV. Confronted by Sebastian with the evidence, Constance confesses her father-in-law ordered the militia in and the family buried it. She begs Sebastian to wait until after the suffrage bill vote — justice later, the cause first. Beat: love against duty made literal between two women who love each other.

chapters.title: The Third Witness
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The last living witness, an ex-sergeant named Croft, has fled to Portsmouth. Sebastian travels alone, posing as a typist, and finds him drinking himself brave. His testimony names Sir Edmund personally. Beat: triumph curdling — now it isn't just a cover-up, it's a man she eats breakfast near.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias wants to publish immediately; Sebastian insists on completeness — every witness, every page, unimpeachable. They fight bitterly, each accusing the other of vanity dressed as principle. He reveals he may be under watch. Beat: the alliance fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: A Search of the Mews
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The Home Office man searches the carriage house; Sebastian's hidden depositions survive only because Constance lies to protect her — claiming the papers are hers. Mother-daughter intimacy deepens even as betrayal does. Beat: found family asserted in the act of deception.

chapters.title: The Historian's Dinner
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Invited to serve at a dinner where the official historian lectures on 'the Wapping regrettable incident,' Sebastian hears her own collected testimony refuted sentence by sentence, elegantly, to applause. Beat: humiliation transmuted into resolve — this is what winning looks like, and she refuses it.

chapters.title: Croft Recants
chapters.summary: Croft's POV. Bought or frightened, Croft signs a retraction. Sebastian reaches Portsmouth too late and sits with him as he weeps, unable to say whether she hates him. He slips her his original sworn statement anyway, folded inside a hymnal. Beat: mercy inside defeat.

chapters.title: Arrest at the Press
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Police raid Fetter Lane on obscenity pretexts; the presses are smashed and Elias is jailed. Sebastian realizes the raid's true target was the Wapping folio — and that someone told them where it was. Beat: paranoia, loss, the sense of a closing trap.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Face
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. She traces the leak to the Harrows' solicitor, acting for Sir Edmund — but discovers Constance knew of the raid in advance and said nothing, believing prison would shield Elias from worse. Sebastian walks out of the house that had become home. Beat: heartbreak; love against duty at its cruelest.

chapters.title: Everything in One Room
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Hiding in a Bloomsbury boarding house, she assembles the complete case: testimonies, photographs, Croft's hymnal statement, the razored inquest inventory. Elias, released on bail, arrives soaked and contrite. They finish the work together through one long night. Beat: reconciliation as collaboration.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Record
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At a packed public inquiry convened by backbench MPs, Sebastian testifies — not as a lady's driver but under her own name, reading the dead back into the record while the Home Office man watches. Sir Edmund's counsel dismantles nothing; the documents hold. Beat: climax; voice as victory.

chapters.title: Consequences
chapters.summary: Constance's POV. Sir Edmund, exposed, negotiates quiet ruin rather than trial; Constance publicly renounces the family name and funds the republication of the suppressed inquest. She asks Sebastian's forgiveness without asking her return. Beat: justice imperfect but real; grief with dignity.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Wapping
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian and Elias stand on the Wapping docks with Maggie Doyle's daughter, reading the seven names aloud as the tide turns. History, she understands now, happens wherever someone writes it down. Beat: mourning become memorial.

chapters.title: A Letter, Unsealed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epistolary close. Months later, Sebastian — now a paid organizer for the movement, driver of no one — writes an open letter about the couriers and keepers of other people's words, and seals nothing. The final line: some letters are meant to be read by everyone. Beat: resolution; the reader of letters becomes their author.
